page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical AMD EPYC 9T24 cores operating at 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance scoring 3075.37 and Geekbench text processing scoring 2483.0, both placing in the top 25% of tested instances. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 6150.88 and a PassMark CPU score of 7535.23. However, memory bandwidth and multi-threaded scaling present notable tradeoffs. Read-only memory bandwidth is relatively weak, measuring 36.57 GB/sec for large blocks, and Geekbench multi-core and software compilation tests fall into the bottom 25%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable compute performance without the risk of resource contention common in shared-core environments. The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio makes it a resource-dense option for compute-heavy tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. This profile is suitable for single-threaded processing, batch computing, text processing, and lightweight web serving, though it is less optimal for memory-intensive databases or highly parallelized multi-threaded compilation tasks.
